newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan President down sharply on inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan President down sharply on inquiry.

text.p: Taiwan's President Enterprises fell sharply in mid-morning trade on Tuesday on news that one of its group members was being investigated for insider trading and that another had delayed its public stock offering, brokers said.
After 80 minutes, President was down 3.01 percent, or T$1.30, at T$41.90. Trade volume was a heavy 10.99 million shares.
The Securities and Exchange Commission said on Tuesday the initial public stock offering for President Chain Store Corp, originally set for Tuesday, had been delayed indefinitely.
In the same statement, the commission said it was investigating President Securities for possible insider trading.
"The news affected investors' sentiment on President Enterprises and directly contributed to its fall today," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.
President Enterprises had planned to release up to T$2 billion of its shares in its President Chain Store subsidiary on Tuesday.
President Chain Store, which runs the 7-ELEVEN convenience store franchise in Taiwan, was rescheduled for listing at the end of 1996.
